subject: Human Evolution
title: Dmanisi: Earliest Europeans
description: A short lesson to help you apply Dmanisi: Earliest Europeans.

hook.text: A medieval town in Georgia sits atop fossils of the earliest humans known outside Africa: 1.8 million years.

buildup.text: Dmanisi's Homo erectus had small brains and simple tools—far more primitive than expected outside Africa.

discovery.text: Five skulls found there vary wildly, suggesting one species can look very different between individuals.

twist.text: This variation sparked debate: maybe several 'species' in Africa are actually just one variable population.

climax.text: Dmanisi challenged the idea that only advanced hominins could make it out of Africa.

punchline.text: You didn't need a big brain to leave home.

quiz.question: What did the Dmanisi fossils reveal?
options: Primitive hominins left Africa very early
